recipes.name: Pressure Cooker Pork Tenderloin
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste

steps.text: Combine cilantro, olive oil, lime juice, garlic, pepper flakes, and salt in a blender; blend until smooth. Pour into a large resealable plastic bag. Add pork tenderloin to the bag, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator, 8 hours to overnight.

Combine chicken broth and lemon juice in a pressure cooker. Remove tenderloin from marinade, shake off excess, and reserve remaining marinade. Place tenderloin in broth mixture in the pressure cooker; pour reserved marinade over tenderloin.

Seal and lock pressure cooker according to manufacturer's instructions. Cook over high heat to build pressure until the indicator sounds. Reduce heat to medium; cook for 25 minutes. Remove from heat; let stand for 5 minutes. Place pressure cooker under cold running water to help release pressure before unsealing the lid. Slice tenderloin into medallions to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pressure Cooker Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: In this recipe, pork tenderloin is marinated in lime juice, oil, cilantro, and chili flakes before pressure cooking with chicken broth and lemon juice.

review.reviewBody: I'm the submitter of this recipe. We love the tartness of lime mixed with the cilantro so this is a personal favorite. AR edited this before publishing and they say to lay the tenderloin into the lemon juice/broth mixture. I don't do that. My pressure cooker has a "rack" that keeps the meat above the liquid so it doesn't actually sit in the liquid as it cooks. This could affect flavor and texture so I'd be interested in hearing your experience if you cook it right in the liquid. AR also converted my "a good handful" of cilantro leaves into 1/4 cup. I use more than 1/4 cup and I also use a heaping 1/2 teaspoon of the red pepper flakes and a scant 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. As you can see, it's a very flexible recipe! The original idea for the marinade comes from my friend, Angela, with a few modifications.

I liked this enough to take a picture of it! I didn't have lemon so I just used lime juice. I followed Dutchgirl's post more cilantro and red pepper and could have used more. But the meat turned out nice. I did it in an electric cooker for 22 mins then I let it the pressure go down on it's own. It was just right and my roast was 1.74 lbs. I will be making this again.

I was amazed at the pork's tenderness in such a short cooking time. After removing pork, I let it rest in a foil tent then added chopped cabbage, shredded carrots, some strips of bacon to the juices. I pressurized the pot again and cooked cabbage mixture for 2 minutes. Cooled and removed. Made an amazing dinner. Thanks for the recipe.

I needed something kind of fast as I forgot I had this tucked away in the fridge. I threw the ingredients together before I left for the afternoon and let it sit in the marinade until I got home (about 5.5 hours). I cooked the 1.5 lb tenderloin at high pressure for 30 min and let it naturally release. I also placed it on the rack to keep it up out of the juices. It was AWESOME! My 13 year old and I had make ourselves stop eating it so there would be left overs for pork carnita style wraps tomorrow night! I have the other 1.5 lbs marinating in the fridge and plan to freeze it for another meal in a week or two. I used cilantro I had frozen and had to use some garlic powder as I did not have enough fresh garlic.

I used 2 lbs of pork tenderloin as packaged...so 2 pieces. I squeezed 3 fresh limes. I used almost my whole bunch of cilantro which was 1/4 cup packed plus a little extra. I was generous with my red pepper flakes, eazy with my salt. I squeezed 1 fresh lemon. Followed all other measurements. I pressured cooked on high for 20mins and let it naturallly release. We thought it was very good.

I thought it was a great base for a pressure cooker. I didn't use the cilantro and I did wrap in bacon and then brown the bacon completely around the loin. Pressure Cooker: 25 minutes with 1/2 cup beef bone broth made a perfect loin.

Was delicious. I did follow some other suggestions from other reviews and added more cilantro, red pepper flakes and a little more garlic. I let the meat marinate a little over 24 hours (might have been overkill but cooked it a little later than expected). It was very good, im glad i added more of those few ingredients and the meat was very tender with the pressure cooker.
It was so tasty! I cut up the pork before marinating it for 12 hrs in fridge. I cooked it in my slow cooker for 2 hrs on high ,then an additional 30 min on low. Will definitely make again

Really liked this recipe! Had to do some tweaking because my cooker is electric and my tenderloin was 1.15 lb. but it still came out great. I cooked it on high for 19 minutes and used a natural release, otherwise I followed the recipe exactly and really liked the marinade, it made a nice “sauce” for the meat and side. I followed one reviewers suggestion of cabbage and carrot side (next time I will plan for the bacon too) and had a wonderful meal. Will definitely make this again! Thanks!

This was good. I added a little more red pepper than called for, but will still add more. Think I would add more garlic as well. I have a digital pressure cooker and put the roast on the bottom of the pot, not a rack. It took about 35 minutes on high. The meat was very tender and juicy. Will fix again with modifications.

I MUST remember to first read the reviews before trying the recipe! Not only did i fail to use a rack, but I also added a cup of basmati and extra broth to the pot. while it was a little bland, I have plenty of spicy condiments for quick fixes. I will try again with the rack next time.
So good. Didnt have the lime, didnt marinate over night. YET, Very tender and tasty. Made gravey and served with rice and broccoli. Good comfy meal.
Love the recipe but it would be extremely helpful as a beginner to have instructions on how to cook the meat from frozen.
good recipe; great flavor and goes well with home style mashed potatoes and green beans.
Very good!
Turned out really really good. I will be making it again.
Outstanding recipe. The pork was tender enough to cut with a fork. The flavor was amazing. Quick and delicious.

Made this and wow, so many questions and complements, I changed 3-4 things. First I used a 4 lb butt roast rather then the tenderloin. For the marinade I used 1/2 cup of salt and 1/2 cup dark brown sugar, 1tbs 5 spice and marinated about 28 hours. Dried really good and smeared with 1 tbs honey and 1 tbs brown mustard and let sit for 30 minutes. Followed the rest of your directions but just set my electric pressure cooker on meat and timer to 50 minutes plus cooldown. Amazing

Made this today. Terrorized the pork followed recipe & let it marinade overnight. Followed the directions for cooking in pressure cooker. Very easy to follow. It was tender & flavorful. 
It is definitely a keeper & will be making it again.
We really enjoyed this easy recipe. The meat was tender and full of flavor. The juices go well with veggies like asparagus and broccoli. Will make again.
